query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a minor Zr addition to promote the in-situ precipitation of metastable tetragonal ZrO2 particles will enhance the fracture toughness of the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy via transformation toughening while maintaining its large caloric response under applied magnetic and pressure fields.
generation.material_initial_state: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy with excellent caloric performance but poor load-bearing integrity and a tendency to crack.
generation.intervention: Add a low concentration of Zr to the alloy composition and apply a controlled heat-treatment process designed to induce the formation of uniformly dispersed metastable tetragonal ZrO2 precipitates within the matrix.
generation.conditions: Operated under the same applied magnetic and pressure fields and the standard temperature range for caloric applications; mechanical loadings that typically induce cracking.
generation.structural_mediator: In-situ precipitated metastable tetragonal ZrO2 particles acting as transformation-toughening agents.
generation.mechanism: Under mechanical loading, the metastable ZrO2 particles partially transform to a monoclinic phase. This transformation induces crack-tip shielding mechanisms such as crack bridging, deflection, and branching, thereby enhancing fracture toughness without significantly altering the microstructural features critical to the caloric response.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved load-bearing integrity with a significant increase in fracture toughness (e.g., by >20%) while preserving the magnitude of the caloric effect (with less than an approximate 5% change) under the same operating fields and temperature conditions.
generation.baseline: The original alloy exhibits a high caloric response but has poor fracture toughness and load-bearing capacity.
generation.boundary: This intervention is expected to be effective within the typical operational temperature range of the caloric device and under the magnetic and pressure fields applied in service; extreme deviations in fields or temperatures may alter the balance between mechanical and caloric properties.
generation.uncertainty: The precise quantitative impact on caloric performance is uncertain because the addition of Zr and the resulting precipitates might slightly alter the entropy-driven caloric mechanisms. Optimization of Zr concentration and heat treatment parameters will be critical to minimize any adverse effects on the caloric response.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of the base (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy and one set with a minor Zr addition followed by controlled heat treatment to induce ZrO2 precipitation. Test both sets under identical conditions for mechanical load-bearing (fracture toughness tests) and caloric performance (measuring caloric effect under applied magnetic and pressure fields at controlled operating temperatures).
measurements: Fracture toughness (e.g., KIC values) via standardized mechanical testing
Caloric response (e.g., magnetocaloric or barocaloric temperature or entropy changes) under defined field strengths
Microstructural characterization (e.g., TEM/SEM) to confirm the formation and distribution of ZrO2 particles
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Zr-added alloy does not exhibit a statistically significant improvement in fracture toughness (e.g., <20% increase relative to the baseline) or if its caloric response is degraded by more than approximately 5% compared to the base alloy under the same field/temperature conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified.

## Abstract
Despite the extremely high hardness of recently proposed high-entropy carbides (HECs), the low fracture toughness limits their applications in harsh mechanical environment. Here, we introduce a metastability engineering strategy to achieve superhard HECs with enhanced toughness via in-situ metastable particles. This is realized by developing a (WTaNbZrTi)C HEC showing a solid solution matrix with uniformly dispersed in-situ tetragonal and monoclinic ZrO2 particles. Apart from a high hardness of 21.0 GPa, the HEC can obtain an enhanced fracture toughness of 5.89 MPa·m1/2, significantly exceeding the value predicted by rule of mixture and that of other reported HECs. The toughening effect is primarily attributed to the transformation of the metastable tetragonal ZrO2 particles under mechanical loading, which promotes crack tip shielding mechanisms including crack deflection, crack bridging and crack branching. The work demonstrates the concept of using in-situ metastable particles for toughening bulk high-entropy ceramics by taking advantage of their compositional flexibility. ## Abstract
FeCrNiCu based high entropy alloy matrix composites were fabricated with addition of Si and C by vacuum electromagnetic induction melting. The primary goal of this research was to analyze the reaction mechanism, microstructure, mechanical properties at room temperature and strengthening mechanism of the composites with addition of Si and C. The reaction mechanism of powders containing (Si, Ni and C) was analyzed, only one reaction occurred (i.e., Si + C → SiC) and its activation energy is 1302.8 kJ/mol. The new composites consist of a face centered cubic (FCC) structured matrix reinforced by submicron sized SiC particles. The addition of Si and C enhances the hardness from 351.4 HV to 626.4 HV and the tensile strength from 565.5 MPa to 846.0 MPa, accompanied by a slight decrease in the plasticity. The main strengthening mechanisms of SiC/FeCrNiCu composites were discussed based on dislocation strengthening, load bearing effect, Orowan mechanism and solid solution hardening, whose contributions to the tensile strength increase are 58.6%, 6.3%, 14.3% and 20.8%, respectively.
